# Helping Your Midwife Find You

*A short guide from the Riverside Community Midwives team*

## Why This Page Matters

When your baby decides it's time, we want to get to you fast. You don't need to tidy the house for us or make tea. You just need us to find the right front door. This page will help you do that.

We have all been lost before. One of our midwives once drove round a block of flats for twenty minutes before she worked out which one was yours. Flat 14 was not next to flat 13. It was in another building. We're telling you this so you know we're human, and so you can help us avoid the same mistake.

## Before 37 Weeks

Our home birth cover starts from 37 weeks. Before that, please plan to go to the hospital. We tell everyone this at your booking visit, and we know it's easy to forget when you have a lot going on. If you're not sure how many weeks you are, just ask us.

## Parking

Two midwives usually come to a birth, and they often arrive in separate cars. If you can, please keep two parking spaces free near your home.

**Permit zones:** Some streets around Anfield and Kensington are permit zones. Please contact the council to apply for a visitor permit before your due date. If you can't get one, leave a visitor permit or a note on your dashboard so we don't get a ticket. Some of us have had tickets before, and nobody wants that at 3am.

## Making Your Home Easy to Find

- **Give us your full address,** including the flat number and building name if you have one.
- **If your house has only a name** (like "Rosemary Cottage") and no number, tell us the street name and a landmark. A sat nav once took one of our midwives to a chip shop.
- **Put your porch light on at night, please!** Dark streets in winter all look the same.
- **Send us a what3words address or a map pin** on WhatsApp to the birth line phone. This is very helpful.
- **Tie balloons to your gate or front door.** One family did this, and it was the best idea we've ever seen. We found them straight away.
- **Think about a friendly neighbour** who can wave us in if you're on a different floor or in a block of flats.

## Getting In and Moving Around

We carry a lot of equipment: gas and air cylinders, our big bags, and sometimes birthing pool parts. Our arms get tired, so a clear route really helps.

- Please clear the stairs and hallway before labour starts.
- Keep shoes, washing baskets, and toys (especially Lego!) out of the way.
- If we need to use a particular door, please make sure it's unlocked and open.

## Pets

We love animals, honestly. One of our midwives is very fond of a staffie called Pippin, who is extremely pleased to see her every visit. But during labour, please keep pets in another room, ideally with the door shut. Pushing and the birth need quiet, and we don't want anyone getting hurt or distracted.

## When Labour Starts: Call the Birth Line

When labour starts, please phone the **Riverside Birth Line** on **[birth line number]**. Please don't call a midwife's personal mobile. The birth line is answered by whoever is on call, so the right person gets your message.

When you call, tell them:

- your full name and address
- how many weeks pregnant you are
- how far apart your contractions are, if you know
- whether your waters have broken
- anything that worries you

If you're not sure whether it's labour yet, call anyway. We would much rather hear from you early than hear about it late.

## Our Promise to You

We are coming to your home as a friend. We know you're not on show and that your home won't look like a magazine. We just want to help you and your baby. Our job is to find you, support you, and make sure you and your baby are safe. Thank you for letting us into your home.

---

## Fridge Checklist

*Tick these off and stick this on your fridge!*

- ☐ I know I need to go to hospital before 37 weeks
- ☐ I have the Riverside Birth Line number saved in my phone: **[birth line number]**
- ☐ I know to call the birth line, not a midwife's personal mobile
- ☐ I have checked the permit zone rules, or I have a visitor permit ready
- ☐ I have kept two parking spaces free (if possible)
- ☐ I have sent my full address and a what3words or map pin to the birth line
- ☐ My porch light works and I know how to switch it on
- ☐ I have put up balloons, or someone is ready to wave us in
- ☐ The stairs and hallway are clear
- ☐ Pets are ready to go into another room
- ☐ I have a bag ready with my notes, nightwear, and snacks for my partner

---

*Note for you (not part of the handout):*
- *Fill in the birth line number in the two places marked [birth line number].*
- *Please check the 37-week cover date and the permit zone details with Deb or the council before you print, since I can't confirm them.*
- *The Pippin and Lego lines are light and friendly, so cut them if your team wants a more formal tone.*
